September 4 th 2026, 6:54pm , By: Ben Bridge
Saturday evening in Townsville gives us an interesting betting scenario where the home favourite has already achieved its primary objective.
North Queensland’s 24-10 victory over Wests Tigers secured eighth position and locked the Cowboys into the finals. Canberra, meanwhile, were eliminated during Round 25 and had the bye last weekend. Neither side therefore enters with conventional must win motivation. That makes the team lists particularly important.
The Cowboys are without Jeremiah Nanai, Griffin Neame and Zac Laybutt. Robert Derby comes onto the wing, while Coen Hess and John Bateman move into the starting pack.
Canberra is not at full strength either. Ethan Sanders is being rested after playing all 23 games this season, with highly rated youngster Coby Black making his NRL debut at halfback. Zac Hosking and Corey Horsburgh are also out, but Morgan Smithies returns, and the Raiders retain Kaeo Weekes, Ethan Strange, Matt Timoko, Xavier Savage, Josh Papalii and Joseph Tapine.

Tom Dearden’s return was a major positive. The Cowboys captain had missed four matches with an ankle injury and immediately restored some stability to a spine that had been shuffled repeatedly in his absence.

The Toyota Forklifts Canberra Raiders have named their team for Saturday evening's match against the North Queensland Cowboys at Queensland Country Bank Stadium.
Club legend Josh Papalii will play his final match for the club in what will be his 342nd and final appearance for the Green Machine.
Coby Black (halfback) and Malachi Smith (bench) have been named to make their NRL debuts this weekend, while Vena Patuki-Case will make his second appearance for the season after his debut earlier in the year.
Raiders Coach Ricky Stuart said the opportunity has been presented to give some players a chance at NRL level to begin preparations for next year.
“Coby, Malachi and Vena get a chance this week. We don’t want to waste a game regarding our preparation for next season, and all three deserve the chance to see what they can show at NRL level.”
“It will be a special occasion for Coby and Malachi to make their debuts for the club, and Vena will benefit from another opportunity at NRL level.”
“I appreciate Daine, Ethan (Sanders) and Tommy understanding that I am looking at the bigger picture in giving some younger players the opportunity to experience the intensity and physicality of the NRL. All three boys have been tremendous for us all season and will continue to be big parts of this squad moving forward.”
Corey Horsburgh will not make the trip north after undergoing shoulder surgery today, while Savelio Tamale (knee) and Zac Hosking (hamstring) are not named in the squad due to injury.
Noah Martin will replace Zac Hosking in the starting side after returning from a quad injury.
Morgan Smithies comes back into the side after missing last week with concussion, in what will be his final match for the club before departing at the end of the season.

The NRL regular season wraps up this weekend – and there’s less at stake than your average Round 27 with the Top 8 already confirmed.
But the minor premiership is still up for grabs and there’s jostling for other positions, equating to home finals in week one, to unfold.
The final round begins with a dead rubber at Accor Stadium as two of 2025’s top-four outfits wrap up their campaigns.
FORM: The Bulldogs have lost three of their last four, with their finals hopes extinguished thanks to a 24-10 loss to the Panthers last week.
The Broncos have lost 13 of their last 15, following up a comeback win in Canberra with a 46-20 home defeat to the Storm last week.
INS AND OUTS: The Bulldogs are unchanged, though Kurt Mann could be a late inclusion. The Broncos’ only change is on the bench with Blake Mozer replaced by Ben Talty.
KEY MATCH-UP: Payne Haas will be eager to inflict some damage in his last game for the Broncos. Max King and Leo Thompson need to meet Haas and twin tower Xavier Willison head on.
HISTORY: The Broncos have won eight of their last nine against the Bulldogs, including a 32-12 result in Round at Suncorp Stadium.
KEY STAT: The Bulldogs haven’t beaten the Broncos in Sydney since 2019.
VERDICT: While this may be a deflating exercise for the Bulldogs after their finals bid officially ended last week, their form has been strong overall and they showed plenty of backbone against the Panthers.
The Broncos have been gagging for the end of a disastrous title defence for some time and have conceded 30-plus points in five straight games. It’s a road trip this injury-ravaged side doesn’t want to be on.

items.title: ‘Godsend’ or major risk? Round of sidelined stars might not matter - Nine.com.au
items.snippet: ‘Godsend’ or major risk? Round of sidelined stars might not matter    Nine.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
Phil Gould believes there is “risk” involved with resting players in the final round of the season, while Brad Fittler believes it will be a “godsend” for the Roosters .
Speaking on Nine’s Freddy and The Eighth this week, the former Roosters skipper had no problem with the club resting nine players and believes it would hold them in good stead heading into September, especially without Sam Walker .
Sam Walker is sidelined with an ankle injury. Getty Images
“Not at all - what they are relying on is their big-game experience,” Fittler said.
“They’ve lost their last two games, but they’re saying ‘you know what, let’s get healthy’. Being healthy is better than one game against South Sydney, which is gonna be a grind and a tough game.
“I think what Robbo [Trent Robinson] has done is the right thing, he’s thinking about winning a comp. To get a week off at this time of the year, especially considering where the Roosters are at, is a godsend for them.”
Gould sees things a little bit differently and believes top-four teams resting their star players in the final round of the regular season can be fraught with danger.
“Resting players in the last round has never been a good formula,” he said on Wide World of Sports’ Six Tackles With Gus .
Read more
Gould’s next test after two players’ bad luck bent Dogs out of shape
“If you finish in the top-four and rest players in the final round, the risk is if you win week one of the finals, you then get another fortnight off and you go into a preliminary final having one game in a month and that’s really hard to manage.
“A week off at this time of year is great, but if you get two of them back-to-back like that, that can be hard to manage and you can be left a little bit rusty.”
Rabbitohs star Cody Walker also warned his rivals – not that he would care what the Roosters do with their premiership plans – telling The Sydney Morning Herald that he “felt a lot worse” after an unplanned week off due to suspension.
Canberra rested most of their team in the final round of 2025 after securing the minor premiership, only to go out in straight-sets in the finals.
As debate around resting players and whether it’s the right option continues, with the way the finals picture is shaping up, how much will it really matter?
Going into round 27, the top-eight is already locked away , with a few potential changes inside of it depending on results this weekend.
In fact, the only positions that are likely to alter are the top-two, with the Warriors and Panthers locked in a tight battle for the NRL minor premiership.
As it stands, the Warriors are ahead of Penrith on points differential by a single point after last weekend’s high-scoring win over Newcastle.
This week, the high-flying Wahs will host the Sea Eagles, while the second-placed Panthers will host the Wests Tigers, with the coveted JJ Giltinan Shield still very much in the balance, even if both teams record victories.
It’s been a year to remember for the Warriors. Getty Images
Andrew Webster and Ivan Cleary have both named strong outfits – the Warriors will sit out hooker Wayde Egan and back-rower Kurt Capewell, while the Panthers haven’t rested any of their big guns at this stage and have co-captain Isaah Yeo on the extended bench as he recovers from a pectoral injury .
Penrith’s hopes of the minor premiership, and what coach Cleary does with his final team, could hinge on the Warriors vs Manly result on Saturday.
If the first-placed Warriors can record a convincing win and put a decent buffer in terms of points differential, Penrith may decide to rest some players if Cleary thinks chasing down the deficit would be too big an ask on Sunday afternoon.
If it’s a close game between the Warriors and Sea Eagles – or if Manly manage to pull off an upset – the Panthers will likely trot out as many of their high-profile players as possible and zero in on beating the Tigers.
